results.title: dependent. Some variants (Zhuang et al., 2023b) further leverage generation likelihood as a relevance score. However, pointwise approaches fail to model interactions among candidates, making them less effective at resolving uncertainty or producing globally consistent top-k rankings. **Listwise methods** (Sun et al., 2023) enable joint evaluation of multiple candidates in a single query, which helps mitigate ranking inconsistency. Approaches like TourRank (Chen et al., 2025) adopt tournament-style aggregation to extend listwise scoring. Despite these benefits, listwise methods still suffer from context length constraints and positional bias (Liu et al., 2024b), especially for long candidate sets. **Pairwise methods** (Qin et al., 2024) improve local comparison quality by directly modeling relative preferences between document pairs. Advanced systems like PRP-Graph (Luo et al., 2024) further exploit graph structures to aggregate pairwise signals. Nevertheless, the repeated comparisons lead to high token usage and substantial inference latency. **Setwise methods** (Zhuang et al., 2024; Podolak et al., 2025) improve efficiency by evaluating small subsets at a time, but discard fine-grained preference information, such as full relevance logits thereby under-utilizing the models capacity.

item.text: {"text":"Stronger pairwise separation does not explicitly model the top-10 cutoff. [SoftmaxLoss@K (KDD 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05673) introduces quantile-based truncation and a smooth NDCG@K surrogate, offering a tractable loss-level alternative without replacing NextItNet. Its guarantees concern NDCG@K, not HR@10. [Differentiable Fast Top-K (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.11472) instead approximates top-K membership directly with an O(n) operator; evidence comes from cascade recommendation, so transfer to next-item prediction remains unproven.\n\nSampling matters when estimating ranks: [Subbiah et al. (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06371) show that correcting sampled-rank bias improves batch WARP and LambdaRank training. Catalog-rank correction should not automatically be applied here: the pinned objective ranks one positive against 99 unique negatives, rather than the full catalog. With one relevant item, HR@10 equals Recall@10 and depends only on crossing the tenth-position boundary. A practical experimental hypothesis is to retain one NextItNet per category, compare sampled listwise cross-entropy against a smooth top-10-membership loss on independently sampled training candidate sets matching the evaluator’s sampling rule, and select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. This targets the actual cutoff more directly than increasing pairwise margins; improvement remains an empirical question."}
